name: sqlkit
description: SQLite helpers over db: a parameters-only query builder, keyset pagination, upserts, batched inserts, up/down migrations with checksums, test fixtures

api.name: Value
api.sig: pub type Value = SqlNull | SqlInt{v: Int} | SqlReal{v: F64} | SqlText{v: Str} | SqlBool{v: Bool} | SqlTime{v: Time} | SqlBlob{v: Bytes} | SqlDec{v: Dec} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A value bound to a `?` placeholder. `db.query` needs one element type in a non-literal parameter
list, so every value is sent as text (`Opt[Str]`) behind a typed placeholder: `CAST(? AS
INTEGER)` for `SqlInt` and `SqlBool`, `CAST(? AS REAL)` for `SqlReal`, `unhex(?)` for
`SqlBlob`, `?` for text, times (ISO 8601 with milliseconds, as the stdlib binds them) and
decimals, and `NULL` for `SqlNull`. The column receives the same type as with a native binding.

api.name: vint
api.sig: fn vint(n: Int) -> Value
api.doc: An integer value.

api.name: vreal
api.sig: fn vreal(x: F64) -> Value
api.doc:
A real value. Infinities and NaN can't be stored by SQLite and are rejected when the query is
built.

api.name: vtext
api.sig: fn vtext(s: Str) -> Value
api.doc: A text value.

api.name: vbool
api.sig: fn vbool(b: Bool) -> Value
api.doc: A boolean value, stored as 0 or 1.

api.name: vtime
api.sig: fn vtime(t: Time) -> Value
api.doc:
A time, stored as ISO 8601 text with milliseconds (`2026-10-15T09:30:00.000Z`), so text order
is time order, exactly as the stdlib binds a `Time`.

api.name: vblob
api.sig: fn vblob(b: Bytes) -> Value
api.doc: A blob value.

api.name: vdec
api.sig: fn vdec(d: Dec) -> Value
api.doc: A decimal, stored as its text (`12.50`), as the stdlib binds a `Dec`.

api.name: vnull
api.sig: fn vnull() -> Value
api.doc: The NULL value.

api.name: vopt
api.sig: fn vopt(o: Opt[Value]) -> Value
api.doc: `none` as NULL, `some(v)` as `v`: `vopt(email.map(vtext))`.

api.name: SqlkitErr
api.sig: pub type SqlkitErr = BadIdent{name: Str, why: Str} | BadQuery{msg: Str} | BadCursor{msg: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Why a statement could not be built: an identifier that is not allowed, a statement that is not
well formed (or is unsafe, such as an UPDATE without WHERE), or a pagination cursor that does
not belong to the query.

api.name: Query
api.sig: pub type Query = {sql: Str, params: List[Opt[Str]]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
SQL text and its parameters, ready for `db.query[T](c, q.sql, q.params)`, `db.one`, `db.opt`
or `db.exec`.

api.name: placeholder
api.sig: fn placeholder(v: Value) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The placeholder and parameter for a value; see `Value`.

api.name: is_keyword
api.sig: fn is_keyword(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` is one of SQLite's 147 keywords, in any case. The builder quotes every identifier,
so a column named `order` or `key` works; use this when you write SQL by hand.

api.name: ident_problem
api.sig: fn ident_problem(s: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
Why `s` is not allowed as a plain identifier, or none: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits and
underscores, not starting with a digit, and not in SQLite's reserved `sqlite_` namespace.

api.name: is_ident
api.sig: fn is_ident(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` is a valid plain identifier (see `ident_problem`).

api.name: quote_ident
api.sig: fn quote_ident(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` as a quoted SQLite identifier: double quotes around it, with each `"` doubled. This is safe
for any text; the builder uses it only on identifiers that passed `ident_problem`.

api.name: column_sql
api.sig: fn column_sql(s: Str) -> Str ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc:
The SQL for one select-list column, checked: `*`, `t.*`, `name`, `t.name`, or any of those
names followed by ` as alias`.

api.name: name_sql
api.sig: fn name_sql(s: Str) -> Str ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The SQL for a table or column name, `name` or `qualifier.name`, checked and quoted.

api.name: Op
api.sig: pub type Op = OpEq | OpNe | OpLt | OpLe | OpGt | OpGe derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A comparison operator.

api.name: Cond
api.sig: pub type Cond = Compare{col: Str, op: Op, v: Value} | CompareCols{a: Str, op: Op, b: Str} | RowCompare{cols: List[Str], op: Op, vs: List[Value]} | InList{col: Str, vs: List[Value], negated: Bool} | Like{col: Str, pattern: Str, negated: Bool} | NullTest{col: Str, negated: Bool} | Between{col: Str, lo: Value, hi: Value, negated: Bool} | AllOf{cs: List[Cond]} | AnyOf{cs: List[Cond]} | Negate{c: Cond} | RawCond{sql: Str, args: List[Value]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A WHERE condition. Build them with the functions below (`eq`, `in_list`, `all_of`, ...); every
value becomes a parameter.

api.name: eq
api.sig: fn eq(col: Str, v: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col = v`. Comparing with NULL is never true in SQL: use `is_null` for that.

api.name: ne
api.sig: fn ne(col: Str, v: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col <> v`.

api.name: lt
api.sig: fn lt(col: Str, v: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col < v`.

api.name: le
api.sig: fn le(col: Str, v: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col <= v`.

api.name: gt
api.sig: fn gt(col: Str, v: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col > v`.

api.name: ge
api.sig: fn ge(col: Str, v: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col >= v`.

api.name: cols_compare
api.sig: fn cols_compare(a: Str, op: Op, b: Str) -> Cond
api.doc: `a op b` for two columns, such as `excluded.version > items.version` in an upsert.

api.name: row_compare
api.sig: fn row_compare(cols: List[Str], op: Op, vs: List[Value]) -> Cond
api.doc:
`(c1, c2, ...) op (v1, v2, ...)`, SQLite's row-value comparison (lexicographic), which can use an
index on those columns.

api.name: in_list
api.sig: fn in_list(col: Str, vs: List[Value]) -> Cond
api.doc: `col IN (v1, v2, ...)`. An empty list matches nothing.

api.name: not_in
api.sig: fn not_in(col: Str, vs: List[Value]) -> Cond
api.doc:
`col NOT IN (v1, v2, ...)`. An empty list matches every row. As in SQL, a NULL in the list
makes the test unknown (false) for every row.

api.name: like
api.sig: fn like(col: Str, pattern: Str) -> Cond
api.doc:
`col LIKE pattern ESCAPE '\'` with a pattern you wrote, where `%` and `_` are wildcards (escape
literal text with `escape_like`). SQLite's LIKE ignores ASCII case.

api.name: not_like
api.sig: fn not_like(col: Str, pattern: Str) -> Cond
api.doc: `col NOT LIKE pattern ESCAPE '\'`.

api.name: escape_like
api.sig: fn escape_like(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the LIKE wildcards `%` and `_` and the escape character `\` escaped, so it matches
itself literally.

api.name: like_substr
api.sig: fn like_substr(col: Str, s: Str) -> Cond
api.doc: Rows whose `col` contains `s` literally (ASCII case ignored).

api.name: like_prefix
api.sig: fn like_prefix(col: Str, s: Str) -> Cond
api.doc: Rows whose `col` starts with `s` literally (ASCII case ignored).

api.name: like_suffix
api.sig: fn like_suffix(col: Str, s: Str) -> Cond
api.doc: Rows whose `col` ends with `s` literally (ASCII case ignored).

api.name: is_null
api.sig: fn is_null(col: Str) -> Cond
api.doc: `col IS NULL`.

api.name: not_null
api.sig: fn not_null(col: Str) -> Cond
api.doc: `col IS NOT NULL`.

api.name: between
api.sig: fn between(col: Str, lo: Value, hi: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col BETWEEN lo AND hi`, both ends included.

api.name: not_between
api.sig: fn not_between(col: Str, lo: Value, hi: Value) -> Cond
api.doc: `col NOT BETWEEN lo AND hi`.

api.name: all_of
api.sig: fn all_of(cs: List[Cond]) -> Cond
api.doc: Every condition holds; an empty list is true.

api.name: any_of
api.sig: fn any_of(cs: List[Cond]) -> Cond
api.doc: At least one condition holds; an empty list is false.

api.name: negate
api.sig: fn negate(c: Cond) -> Cond
api.doc: `NOT (c)`.

api.name: raw
api.sig: fn raw(sql: Str, args: List[Value]) -> Cond
api.doc:
An escape hatch: SQL you wrote, with one bare `?` per argument (outside quoted text), such as
`raw("lower(email) = ?", [vtext(e)])`. Each `?` becomes the argument's typed placeholder. Never
build `sql` from input; that is what the arguments are for.

api.name: cond_sql
api.sig: fn cond_sql(c: Cond) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The SQL and parameters of a condition.

api.name: Nulls
api.sig: pub type Nulls = NullsDefault | NullsFirst | NullsLast derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Where NULLs sort.

api.name: Order
api.sig: pub type Order = {col: Str, desc: Bool, nulls: Nulls} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One ORDER BY term.

api.name: asc
api.sig: fn asc(col: Str) -> Order
api.doc: Ascending by `col`.

api.name: desc
api.sig: fn desc(col: Str) -> Order
api.doc: Descending by `col`.

api.name: nulls_first
api.sig: fn nulls_first(o: Order) -> Order
api.doc: The same order with NULLs first.

api.name: nulls_last
api.sig: fn nulls_last(o: Order) -> Order
api.doc: The same order with NULLs last.

api.name: Select
api.sig: pub type Select = {table: Str, column_list: List[Str], is_distinct: Bool, where_cond: Opt[Cond], order_terms: List[Order], row_limit: Opt[Int], row_offset: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A SELECT. Build one with `select` and the functions after it, or with a literal and `with`.

api.name: select
api.sig: fn select(table: Str) -> Select
api.doc: `SELECT * FROM table`.

api.name: columns
api.sig: fn columns(s: Select, cols: List[Str]) -> Select
api.doc: The columns to select (see `column_sql`); an empty list is `*`.

api.name: distinct
api.sig: fn distinct(s: Select) -> Select
api.doc: SELECT DISTINCT.

api.name: select_where
api.sig: fn select_where(s: Select, c: Cond) -> Select
api.doc: Adds a condition, joined with AND to any condition already there.

api.name: order_by
api.sig: fn order_by(s: Select, os: List[Order]) -> Select
api.doc: Adds ORDER BY terms after those already there.

api.name: limit
api.sig: fn limit(s: Select, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> Select
api.doc: At most `n` rows.

api.name: offset
api.sig: fn offset(s: Select, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> Select
api.doc: Skips the first `n` rows (`LIMIT -1 OFFSET n` when there is no limit).

api.name: select_sql
api.sig: fn select_sql(s: Select) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The SQL and parameters of a SELECT.

api.name: count_sql
api.sig: fn count_sql(s: Select) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc:
`SELECT count(*)` over the rows `s` selects, ignoring its order, limit and offset; read it with
`db.one[Int]`.

api.name: exists_sql
api.sig: fn exists_sql(s: Select) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: `SELECT EXISTS (...)` over the rows `s` selects, 0 or 1; read it with `db.one[Bool]`.

api.name: Conflict
api.sig: pub type Conflict = ConflictFail | DoNothing{target: List[Str]} | DoUpdate{target: List[Str], from_excluded: List[Str], assign: List[(Str, Value)], only_if: Opt[Cond]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What an INSERT does when a row conflicts with a unique key: fail (the default), do nothing, or
update. `DoUpdate` sets each of `from_excluded` to the value the insert proposed
(`excluded.col`), each pair of `assign` to a value, and applies only where `only_if` holds.

api.name: Insert
api.sig: pub type Insert = {into: Str, cols: List[Str], rows: List[List[Value]], on_conflict: Conflict, returning_cols: List[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: An INSERT of one or more rows.

api.name: insert
api.sig: fn insert(table: Str, cols: List[Str]) -> Insert
api.doc: `INSERT INTO table (cols...)` with no rows yet.

api.name: values
api.sig: fn values(i: Insert, row: List[Value]) -> Insert
api.doc: Adds a row; it must have one value per column.

api.name: values_all
api.sig: fn values_all(i: Insert, rows: List[List[Value]]) -> Insert
api.doc: Adds rows.

api.name: on_conflict_nothing
api.sig: fn on_conflict_nothing(i: Insert, target: List[Str]) -> Insert
api.doc: `ON CONFLICT (target) DO NOTHING`; an empty target is any uniqueness conflict.

api.name: on_conflict_update
api.sig: fn on_conflict_update(i: Insert, target: List[Str], set_cols: List[Str]) -> Insert
api.doc: `ON CONFLICT (target) DO UPDATE SET c = excluded.c` for each of `set_cols`.

api.name: upsert
api.sig: fn upsert(table: Str, cols: List[Str], row: List[Value], key: List[Str]) -> Insert
api.doc:
The upsert of `row` into `table` keyed by `key`: inserts it, or updates every other column of
the existing row.

api.name: insert_returning
api.sig: fn insert_returning(i: Insert, cols: List[Str]) -> Insert
api.doc: RETURNING these columns (see `column_sql`); read the rows with `db.query[T]` or `db.one[T]`.

api.name: insert_sql
api.sig: fn insert_sql(i: Insert) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The SQL and parameters of an INSERT.

api.name: insert_chunks
api.sig: fn insert_chunks(i: Insert, max_params: Int where _ > 0) -> List[Insert] ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc:
The insert split into inserts of consecutive rows, each with at most `max_params` parameters
(SQLite's limit is 32766). A single row with more parameters is an error.

api.name: max_params
api.sig: fn max_params() -> Int
api.doc: SQLite's limit on parameters in one statement.

api.name: insert_batch
api.sig: fn insert_batch(c: Db, i: Insert) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc:
Inserts all the rows of `i` in one transaction, in statements under SQLite's parameter limit,
and returns the number of rows changed.

api.name: Update
api.sig: pub type Update = {table: Str, set_list: List[(Str, Value)], where_cond: Opt[Cond], returning_cols: List[Str], all_rows: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: An UPDATE. Without a condition it is refused unless `all_rows` is set (`update_all`).

api.name: update
api.sig: fn update(table: Str, sets: List[(Str, Value)]) -> Update
api.doc: `UPDATE table SET col = value, ...`.

api.name: update_where
api.sig: fn update_where(u: Update, c: Cond) -> Update
api.doc: Adds a condition, joined with AND to any condition already there.

api.name: update_all
api.sig: fn update_all(u: Update) -> Update
api.doc: Allows the update to change every row (no WHERE).

api.name: update_returning
api.sig: fn update_returning(u: Update, cols: List[Str]) -> Update
api.doc: RETURNING these columns.

api.name: update_sql
api.sig: fn update_sql(u: Update) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The SQL and parameters of an UPDATE.

api.name: Delete
api.sig: pub type Delete = {table: Str, where_cond: Opt[Cond], returning_cols: List[Str], all_rows: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A DELETE. Without a condition it is refused unless `all_rows` is set (`delete_all`).

api.name: delete
api.sig: fn delete(table: Str) -> Delete
api.doc: `DELETE FROM table`.

api.name: delete_where
api.sig: fn delete_where(d: Delete, c: Cond) -> Delete
api.doc: Adds a condition, joined with AND to any condition already there.

api.name: delete_all
api.sig: fn delete_all(d: Delete) -> Delete
api.doc: Allows the delete to remove every row (no WHERE).

api.name: delete_returning
api.sig: fn delete_returning(d: Delete, cols: List[Str]) -> Delete
api.doc: RETURNING these columns.

api.name: delete_sql
api.sig: fn delete_sql(d: Delete) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The SQL and parameters of a DELETE.

api.name: exec
api.sig: fn exec(c: Db, x: Query) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Runs a statement that returns no rows (`db.exec` with its parameters) and returns the number of
rows changed.

api.name: Keyset
api.sig: pub type Keyset = {base: Select, keys: List[Order], page_size: Int where _ > 0} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Keyset (seek) pagination over `base` ordered by `keys`: each page starts after (or before) the
key of a row instead of at an offset, so pages are stable under inserts and cost the same deep
into the table. The keys must identify a row (end them with the primary key) and must not be
NULL; directions may be mixed. `base` gives the table, columns and filter, and must not set its
own order, limit or offset.

api.name: keyset
api.sig: fn keyset(base: Select, keys: List[Order], page_size: Int where _ > 0) -> Keyset
api.doc: Keyset pagination of `base` by `keys`, `page_size` rows a page.

api.name: KeyPage
api.sig: pub type KeyPage[T] = {items: List[T], after: Opt[Str], before: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A page: its rows in key order, the cursor for the page after it (`after`, when there may be
more rows) and the cursor for the page before it (`before`, when this page was reached through a
cursor).

api.name: cursor
api.sig: fn cursor(k: Keyset, key: List[Value]) -> Str ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc:
The opaque cursor for a row whose key columns hold `key` (one value per key, in order). It is
base64url JSON, not signed: a changed cursor can only select another page of the same query.

api.name: decode_cursor
api.sig: fn decode_cursor(k: Keyset, c: Str) -> List[Value] ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The key values in a cursor, checked against the keyset it must belong to.

api.name: keyset_sql
api.sig: fn keyset_sql(k: Keyset, after: Opt[Str]) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc:
The query for the page after `after` (the first page for `none`), ordered by the keys, with one
row more than a page so `keyset_page` can tell whether more follow.

api.name: keyset_before_sql
api.sig: fn keyset_before_sql(k: Keyset, before: Opt[Str]) -> Query ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc:
The query for the page before `before` (the last page for `none`). Its rows come in reverse
key order; `keyset_page_before` puts them back.

api.name: keyset_page
api.sig: fn keyset_page[T](k: Keyset, after: Opt[Str], rows: List[T], key: T -> List[Value]) -> KeyPage[T] ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The page from the rows `keyset_sql(k, after)` returned; `key` gives a row's key values.

api.name: keyset_page_before
api.sig: fn keyset_page_before[T](k: Keyset, before: Opt[Str], rows: List[T], key: T -> List[Value]) -> KeyPage[T] ! fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The page from the rows `keyset_before_sql(k, before)` returned, in key order.

api.name: Migration
api.sig: pub type Migration = {version: Int where _ > 0, name: Str, up: Str, down: Str} derive Eq, Show

api.name: migration
api.sig: fn migration(version: Int where _ > 0, name: Str, up: Str, down: Str) -> Migration
api.doc: A migration.

api.name: MigrateErr
api.sig: pub type MigrateErr = DuplicateVersion{version: Int} | UnorderedVersion{version: Int} | ChangedMigration{version: Int, name: Str} | UnknownApplied{version: Int} | OutOfOrder{version: Int} | Irreversible{version: Int, name: Str} | NoSuchTarget{version: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Why migrations can't run: the list is not in order or repeats a version; an applied migration
was edited since (its checksum differs) or is no longer in the list; a pending one is older
than one already applied; a step down has no `down`; or the target version is not in the list.

api.name: Direction
api.sig: pub type Direction = StepUp | StepDown derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Whether a step applies or undoes its migration.

api.name: Step
api.sig: pub type Step = {version: Int, name: Str, direction: Direction, sql: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One step of a plan: the migration, which way, and the SQL that runs.

api.name: MigrationState
api.sig: pub type MigrationState = Applied{at: Str} | Pending | Changed{at: Str} | Missing{at: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Where a migration stands in a database: applied (with the time it was applied), pending,
applied but edited since, or applied but missing from the list.

api.name: MigrationStatus
api.sig: pub type MigrationStatus = {version: Int, name: Str, state: MigrationState} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One migration's state.

api.name: migrations_table
api.sig: fn migrations_table() -> Str
api.doc: The table sqlkit records applied migrations in (db.migrate uses its own, `sspur_migrations`).

api.name: checksum
api.sig: fn checksum(m: Migration) -> Str
api.doc:
The SHA-256 of a migration's `up` SQL, in hex: what is recorded when it is applied and compared
afterwards. Editing `down` later is allowed; editing `up` is `ChangedMigration`.

api.name: validate
api.sig: fn validate(ms: List[Migration]) -> Unit ! fail[MigrateErr]
api.doc: Checks that versions increase strictly along the list.

api.name: latest
api.sig: fn latest(ms: List[Migration]) -> Int
api.doc: The newest version in the list, or 0 for none.

api.name: current_version
api.sig: fn current_version(c: Db) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The newest applied version, or 0 for none.

api.name: status
api.sig: fn status(c: Db, ms: List[Migration]) -> List[MigrationStatus] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Each migration of the list with its state, then applied versions the list doesn't have.

api.name: plan
api.sig: fn plan(c: Db, ms: List[Migration], target: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[Step] ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[MigrateErr]
api.doc:
The steps that would bring the database to `target` (0 undoes everything), without changing
anything: the dry run. Up steps run oldest first, down steps newest first.

api.name: migrate_to
api.sig: fn migrate_to(c: Db, ms: List[Migration], target: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[Step] ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[MigrateErr]
api.doc:
Brings the database to `target`: applies or undoes migrations, each step in its own
transaction with its record, and returns the steps that ran. The whole plan is checked before
the first step, so an error changes nothing. A step another process ran meanwhile is skipped.

api.name: migrate_latest
api.sig: fn migrate_latest(c: Db, ms: List[Migration]) -> List[Step] ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[MigrateErr]
api.doc: Applies every pending migration.

api.name: rollback
api.sig: fn rollback(c: Db, ms: List[Migration], n: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[Step] ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[MigrateErr]
api.doc: Undoes the newest `n` applied migrations.

api.name: test_db
api.sig: fn test_db(ms: List[Migration]) -> Db ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[MigrateErr]
api.doc: A fresh in-memory database with every migration applied.

api.name: load_fixtures
api.sig: fn load_fixtures(c: Db, fixtures: List[Insert]) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: Inserts fixture rows in one transaction and returns the number of rows changed.

api.name: row_count
api.sig: fn row_count(c: Db, table: Str) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[SqlkitErr]
api.doc: The number of rows in `table`.

api.name: rolled_back
api.sig: fn rolled_back[e](c: Db, f: () -> Bool ! e) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr], e
api.doc:
Runs a test body inside a transaction that is always rolled back, and returns its result, so
tests can share one database without seeing each other's writes. Nested `db.tx` calls in `f`
become savepoints. (The result is a `Bool`, what a test needs: `db.tx` can't yet be wrapped
by a function generic in its result type.)
